brief: Design an interface for a "Memory Auction House" where users bid on their own forgotten memories using emotional currency — each memory appears as a floating, semi-transparent polaroid that phases in

dominant_strengths: Clean restrained typography with consistent hierarchy between titles, time remaining, and amber-priced emotional currency values
Disciplined dark canvas with grid alignment and a subtle status bar that hints at a system worth exploring
dominant_weaknesses: Empty gray placeholder rectangles betray zero craft on the core artifact — the polaroid memory itself is missing
Brief demands floating, semi-transparent, phasing polaroids and emotional currency, yet the output is a generic auction grid with dollar signs
No emotional texture: no grain, blur, vignette, handwriting, or temporal decay cues that would evoke memory or nostalgia
fix_priorities: Replace placeholder cards with actual polaroid artifacts: tilted, translucent, soft-shadowed, with imagery or evocative abstractions and tape/handwriting
Swap dollar amounts for an emotional currency system (tears, joy units, regret tokens) with custom glyphs and meters
Introduce phase-in motion language and depth layering so memories feel summoned rather than listed
Add atmospheric treatment — film grain, warm bloom, or fading edges — to anchor the nostalgic concept
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral scanning works adequately, but visceral wonder and reflective meaning are both starved by the literal e-commerce treatment.
rationale.intent_fit: It reads as a generic auction marketplace skin and ignores nearly every poetic affordance the brief requested.
